method: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation' (last updated March 2020). Every claim is a paraphrase backed by anchors (scripts/anchor.py): verify.py --source re-finds each anchored span in a fresh copy of the source, checks the claim's numbers against it and rejects copying. LICENCE: © The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne; Terms clause 5.2, personal use only; paraphrased and hash-anchored (read at RCH Terms and Conditions, clause 5.2 (rch.org.au)). The source's words are NOT reproduced here. Edition 2.0 rebuilds the Wave 1 hand-written edition (verbatim quotes) as paraphrase against the page fetched 2026-09-24. Every clinical claim of edition 1.0 is carried over; the last-updated claim now sits in the source date and a banner. The maintenance appendix and both disimpaction schedules are tables rendered as text: each row's values are anchored, but column alignment is a transcription risk, so confirm the grid on the live page before prescribing.

claims.claim: **About 1/3 of children get constipated,** often when solids are introduced, during toilet training, and on starting school.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Constipation symptoms tend to go unreported.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Most children open their bowels at least every 2-3 days;** a breastfed baby may go as seldom as once a week.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Infant dyschezia is not constipation:** healthy babies under 6 months may strain and cry before passing a soft stool. Unless the stool is also hard, it settles on its own.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **The withholding cycle:** a young child who ignores the urge builds up large, hard stools; if passing them hurts, fear follows, then more holding on and more hard stool.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Children with autism spectrum disorder or ADHD are at higher risk** of functional constipation.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Diagnose on clinical grounds.** An internal (rectal) examination and an X-ray are unnecessary.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Talk to a senior clinician before doing any internal examination.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Routine investigations are not needed.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Rome IV functional constipation — 2 or more of these, for at least 1 month (infants) or 2 months (older children):** 2 or fewer stools a week; retentive posturing or excessive deliberate holding (withholding, incomplete emptying); painful or hard stools; stools of large diameter; a large faecal mass in the rectum.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Extra criterion once toilet-trained:** soiling or incontinence at least 1 time a week after toileting skills have been learned.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Examine** the lower back and spine for occult spinal dysraphism or tethered cord, and the lower limbs and gait neurologically.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Red flags:** an infant under 6 weeks (discuss with a senior doctor) · ribbon-like stools (anorectal malformation) · meconium not passed in the first 24 hours, as most babies do (think anorectal malformation or Hirschsprung disease) · weight loss or poor growth · persistent vomiting · an abdominal mass that does not fit with a faecal mass.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Organic causes to keep in mind.** Medical: coeliac disease, hypothyroidism, hypercalcaemia, slow-transit constipation. Surgical: Hirschsprung disease, meconium ileus, anal malformations, spinal cord abnormalities.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Sitting position:** a footstool so the knees sit above the hips; lean forward with elbows resting on knees.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Toilet sits:** three times a day, ideally after meals, each up to 5 minutes. Get the child to push the tummy out, praise them for sitting, and keep toileting a positive experience.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Hold off toilet training until the child passes soft stools without pain.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Check access to toilets,** for example what stops the child using the toilets at school.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Too much cow's milk can crowd out dietary fibre** and worsen constipation in some children.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **More fibre alone does not treat constipation.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Fluids above normal daily maintenance are not needed.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Aim for one soft, easily passed stool every day,** adjusting the dose to get there; medicines are often needed.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Osmotic and lubricant laxatives usually go on for months to years.** Tell parents this is safe and will not make the bowel 'lazy'.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Stopping laxatives too soon is a common reason constipation comes back;** treatment usually lasts several months.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Avoid rectal treatment** (suppositories, enemas).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **First-line choice by age:** under 1 month, Coloxyl drops · 1-12 months, an iso-osmotic laxative (macrogol 3350 with electrolytes) or lactulose · older children, an iso-osmotic laxative or a lubricant (paraffin oil).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Inpatient disimpaction may help** children who withhold stool, have pain on defecation, or have rectal bleeding or fissures.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **For pain from an anal fissure, apply petroleum jelly.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Lactulose (osmotic):** 3-5 mL/day at 1-12 mo; 5-10 mL/day at 1-5 yo; 10-40 mL/day at 5-14 yo. Give larger doses in two (bd).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Coloxyl drops (poloxamer), three times a day:** 0.3 mL under 6 mo; 0.5 mL at 6-18 mo; 0.8 mL from 18 mo-3 yo. With Coloxyl+Senna, the senna is a stimulant — avoid it unless stools are already soft, and only over 2 yo.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Macrogol 3350 + electrolytes sachets, daily:** ½ at 1-12 mo; 1 at 1-6 yo (up to 2/day); 1-2 at 6-12 yo (up to 2/day); 1-4 over 12 yo. PBS listed, no authority needed.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Macrogol 3350 powder (tin with a two-ended scoop, large 17 g, small 8.5 g), daily:** 1 small scoop at 2-6 yo; 1 large scoop at 6-12 yo; 1-2 large scoops over 12 yo.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Paraffin oil (lubricant), per day:** 10-15 mL at 1-6 yo; 15-20 mL at 6-12 yo; up to 40 mL over 12 yo. Orange oily leakage into underwear means the dose should come down. **Avoid with swallowing difficulty (aspiration risk), especially under 6 mo.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Stimulant (sodium picosulfate drops or bisacodyl), at night:** 6 mo-4 yo 0.25 mg/kg (up to 5 mg = 10 drops); 4-10 yo 5-10 drops; over 10 yo 10 drops or 1-2 tablets. Handy when a child cannot manage large liquid volumes. **Not if impacted; may cramp; not for long-term use.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Severe constipation: clear the impaction first, then start maintenance.** Oral outpatient treatment works and is preferred; move straight to maintenance once disimpaction is done.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **A glycerine suppository or Microlax enema is a one-off option only,** and sedation deserves strong consideration.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **On day 4, review whether disimpaction still needs to continue.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Outpatient macrogol 3350 + electrolytes (adult sachets) per day, over days 1-7:** ages 1-6 years → 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4 · ages 6-12 years → 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 6, 6 · ages 12+ → 8 on each of days 1-3 only.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Sachet equivalence:** one adult-strength macrogol 3350 with electrolytes sachet equals 2 Movicol Junior sachets.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Outpatient OsmoLax small scoops (8.5 g) per day, over days 1-7:** ages 2-6 years → 2, 3, 3, 4, 5, 6, 6 · ages 6-12 years → 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 9, 9.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Nasogastric washout:** macrogol/electrolyte solution (Colonlytely, Glycoprep), 1-3 L/day at 25 mL/kg/hr, capped at 400 mL/hr (or lower, depending on the pump).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Give usual maintenance oral fluids as well:** washout solutions add no net fluid, so dehydration is a risk.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Fixed-dose sodium picosulphate:** 4-9 yo, 1 sachet then ½ sachet as the second dose (15 mg/day); over 9 yo, 1 sachet twice daily (20 mg/day).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Not with signs of obstruction or with renal impairment.** Think about stopping once the child passes clear fluid rectally.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Oral medicines given during a washout, or in the hour before it, may be washed through unabsorbed.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **See the GP or paediatrician again within 4 weeks.** Complex or difficult cases, or faecal or urinary incontinence, may warrant a continence or encopresis service.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Consider the local paediatric team when** red flags or suspected organic disease are present; constipation has not resolved after 6 months of optimised outpatient care; or outpatient disimpaction fails and inpatient care is needed.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Constipation', last updated March 2020, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Constipation/, retrieved 2026-09-24
